TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample-Complexity Guarantee for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We propose establishing a non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantee for KernelSHAP by showing that with $m \geq (1 + \delta) 2^d (\ln d)^2$ subsampled rows of $\bm{v}$ and corresponding kernel weights $\bm{W}$, the estimate $\hat{\bm{\phi}}$ satisfies $\|\phi - \hat{\bm{\phi}}\|_2 \leq O(\delta) \|v\|_2$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, where $\bm{\phi}$ is the limiting solution to the constrained least-squares problem.
CONTROLS: We compare our results to existing estimators like LeverageSHAP and study the performance of our bound empirically on various real-world data sets.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The proposed bound should show KernelSHAP's sample efficiency, and the empirical experiments should demonstrate its accuracy relative to other estimators, with potential pitfalls arising in highly noisy data sets.

TITLE: LeverageSHAP Sample-Complexity Reduction via Augmented Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose an extension of LeverageSHAP by augmenting its sampling procedure with additional strategically chosen points, aimed at reducing the overall sample complexity while preserving its non-asymptotic convergence guarantees. We investigate how including a carefully sampled set of 'difficulty' points can improve the estimator's performance by adapting to the local geometry of the value function.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against a 'naive' LeverageSHAP implementation and KernelSHAP, examining their behavior in high-dimensional cases through a battery of real-world experiments on diverse datasets.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The proposed augmentation technique is expected to provide improved accuracy and efficiency in a variety of realistic settings, while also providing novel insights into the nature of the value function and its local structure. In cases where the value function exhibits large sudden drops in prediction, the procedure could experience subpar performance due to over-aggregation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A General Framework for Model-Agnostic Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a broad and flexible framework for estimating Shapley values, encompassing various existing methodologies, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, as special cases. The framework relies on solving a regularized least-squares objective with adaptive weights, which are determined based on the intrinsic properties of the data. This allows for handling different types of value functions and learning Shapley values efficiently even when the value function is ill-behaved.
CONTROLS: We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on a range of real-world datasets, comparing it with various state-of-the-art Shapley value estimators, including the ones proposed in our prior tasks.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Our framework is expected to provide a general and computationally efficient solution for estimating Shapley values in diverse scenarios, with potential applications in model interpretability, sensitivity analysis, and feature attribution. However, its performance might degrade in cases where the underlying value function is highly non-linear or has limited regularity.

TITLE: A General Framework for Model-Agnostic Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: We revise our prior proposal to incorporate additional robustness guarantees, by introducing a data-driven procedure for selecting the optimal regularization parameter, which adapts to the intrinsic properties of the data and value function. This ensures stability and robustness of the estimation process, particularly in challenging scenarios where data quality or value function properties are uncertain or unknown.
CONTROLS: We incorporate extensive experiments to profile the performance of our revised framework under different conditions, providing a nuanced understanding of its strengths and limitations.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: The revised framework is expected to provide a more robust and reliable approach to estimating Shapley values, with improved accuracy and resistance to issues stemming from suboptimal regularization, but it may incur additional computational costs due to the added complexity of the parameter selection procedure.

TITLE: Scalable and Approximate Shapley Value Computation via Manifold Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel, scalable, and approximate approach to computing Shapley values, based on sampling the underlying manifold structure of the data using techniques from dimensionality reduction and manifold learning. This approach enables efficient and accurate estimation of Shapley values, even in high-dimensional settings, by exploiting the geometry and connectivity of the data manifold.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach with state-of-the-art methods, including the revised framework for model-agnostic Shapley value estimation, on a range of real-world datasets and analyze its trade-offs in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
COST: 11000
PREDICTION: Our method is expected to provide an efficient and scalable solution for computing Shapley values, especially in high-dimensional settings, but its performance may degrade in scenarios where the data manifold is highly non-convex or has limited regularity.

TITLE: Interpretable and Aligned Feature Importance via Orthogonal Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to computing Shapley values that takes advantage of the orthogonality between features to provide interpretable and aligned feature importance. This approach enables the practitioner to meaningfully understand the contributions of individual features to the model's predictions, while avoiding issues of feature redundancy and confounding.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach with existing methods for computing Shapley values on a range of real-world datasets, including those with highly correlated features, and analyze its trade-offs in terms of accuracy and interpretability.
COST: 13500
PREDICTION: Our method is expected to provide a novel and insightful perspective on feature importance, with applications in fields such as recommender systems and climate modeling, but its performance may degrade in scenarios where the features are not sufficiently orthogonal.

TITLE: A Certified Bounded Error Estimator for Noisy Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to estimating Shapley values in the presence of noisy data, by developing a certified bounded error estimator that provides a rigorous guarantee on the error between the estimated and true Shapley values. This approach enables practitioners to trust their estimates and make informed decisions without worrying about the impact of noise on the results.
CONTROLS: We analyze the trade-offs between estimator accuracy, computational efficiency, and certification strength, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of real-world datasets with noisy data.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: Our estimator is expected to provide a novel and valuable tool for estimating Shapley values in noisy environments, with applications in fields such as finance and climate modeling, but its performance may degrade in scenarios where the noise level is very high or the data is highly irregular.

TITLE: Unifying and Extending thetoolbox for Shapley Value Estimation: A Comprehensive Comparison and Benchmark
PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive comparison and benchmarking study that unifies and extends the toolbox for Shapley value estimation, evaluating the performance and strengths of existing methods, including the ones proposed in our prior tasks, and introducing new, hybrid approaches that integrate their benefits. This study aims to provide a definitive reference point for practitioners and researchers, facilitating informed decision-making and advancing the field of Shapley value estimation.
CONTROLS: We systematically compare the performance of each approach across a diverse range of real-world datasets and applications, using a battery of metrics and evaluation tasks.
COST: 22000
PREDICTION: Our comprehensive comparison and benchmarking study is expected to provide a definitive evaluation of the existing methods and identify novel opportunities for improvement, influencing the development of future research directions and applications, while also highlighting potential pitfalls and limitations in the existing approaches.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Multimodal Large Language Model for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Develop a variant of the T5-XXL multimodal large language model that takes into account the temporal evolution of the scene by conditioning the attention mechanism on the sequence of satellite images and additional metadata such as satellite sensor information, acquisition dates, and possibly ground-truth changes.
CONTROLS: Use as a baseline a standard T5-XXL model without multimodal input and possibly a change description method that fuses information across images through simple interactions.
COST: 50000
PREDICTION: The model should significantly improve upon existing change description methods by capturing the underlying causal narrative of the changes and provide a coherent temporal storyline. However, its performance may degrade on datasets with variable or uncertain acquisition intervals, as it heavily relies on the precise timing of the images.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Diffusion-Based Future Satellite Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Modify a state-of-the-art diffusion-based image model (e.g., DALL-E or the recently proposed U-Net-based diffusion model) to generate plausible future satellite images by conditioning the model on the historical sequence of satellite images and metadata, and fine-tuning the model on satellite image time series forecasting datasets. The key innovation will be incorporating a temporal consistency loss term to ensure that the generated changes are a logical continuation of the trends and dynamics observed in the historical data.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance to a standard diffusion-based image model without temporal conditioning and a recurrent neural network (RNN) based model specifically designed for temporal forecasting.
COST: 75000
PREDICTION: The model should be able to generate realistic and temporally consistent future satellite images and improve upon traditional forecasting methods. However, due to the complexity of the temporal dynamics in satellite image time series, the model may require a significant amount of fine-tuning data and computational resources.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel evaluation metric, the Temporal Consistency Score (TCS), that measures how well the predicted changes align with the historical trends and dynamics in the satellite image time series. TCS will be calculated by comparing the predicted changes with the actual changes in the future images, taking into account the uncertainty and variability inherent in satellite image acquisition.
CONTROLS: Use TCS in conjunction with standard image quality metrics to evaluate the performance of the models proposed in prior research questions.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: The TCS metric should provide a more comprehensive evaluation of temporal consistency in satellite image forecasting models, allowing researchers to identify the strengths and weaknesses of these models. However, its effectiveness may depend on the availability of high-quality ground-truth data for evaluating the actual changes in the satellite images.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Insight-Guided Temporal Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a framework for insight-guided temporal forecasting that uses explainability techniques (e.g., feature importance or attention visualizations) to identify the key temporal factors driving changes in the satellite image time series. This framework will allow researchers to understand why certain changes occur and to what extent they are driven by temporal factors, and to use this knowledge to improve the temporal consistency and accuracy of the forecasts.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the insight-guided framework with a standard diffusion-based model and a model trained with a temporal consistency loss term.
COST: 100000
PREDICTION: The insight-guided framework should provide valuable insights into the temporal dynamics of the satellite image time series and lead to improved temporal consistency and accuracy in the forecasts. However, its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the explainability techniques used and the difficulty of the forecasting task.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Multimodal Large Language Model for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Revise the variant of the T5-XXL multimodal large language model to incorporate a hierarchical attention mechanism that allows it to focus on different levels of abstractions in the satellite image sequence (e.g., regional, local, and pixel-level) and to reason about the temporal evolution of the scene at each level of abstraction. This will enable the model to provide more detailed and nuanced descriptions of the key dynamic changes that occurred over the observation period.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the revised model with the original version and a standard T5-XXL model without multimodal input.
COST: 40000
PREDICTION: The revised model should significantly improve upon existing change description methods by capturing the underlying causal narrative of the changes at multiple levels of abstraction. However, its performance may suffer from increased computational complexity, making it more challenging to fine-tune and optimize.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Semantics-Aware Temporal Modeling
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel temporal modeling approach that incorporates semantic graph convolutional networks to model the abstract relationships between the key dynamic changes in the satellite image sequence. This approach will allow the model to capture the underlying causal narrative of the changes and to reason about the temporal evolution of the scene at a semantic level.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the semantics-aware temporal modeling approach with a standard diffusion-based model and a model trained with a temporal consistency loss term.
COST: 125000
PREDICTION: The semantics-aware temporal modeling approach should lead to significant improvements in the accuracy and temporal consistency of the forecasts. However, its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the semantic graph and the availability of labeled data for training and validation.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a multi-task learning framework that trains a single model to perform both temporal change description and forecasting tasks simultaneously. This will allow the model to leverage the shared information between the two tasks and to reason about the temporal evolution of the scene in a more holistic way.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the multi-task learning framework with a standard model trained for each task separately.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: The multi-task learning framework should lead to significant improvements in both tasks by sharing knowledge and jointly optimizing the model's parameters. However, its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the tasks' datasets and the difficulty of the two tasks.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Transfer Learning for Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Propose a temporally consistent transfer learning approach that leverages the knowledge and temporal dynamics learned from one domain or dataset to adapt to another domain or dataset. This will enable the model to generalize across different domains and to reason about the temporal evolution of the scene in a more robust and consistent way.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the temporally consistent transfer learning approach with a standard transfer learning approach and a model trained from scratch for each domain.
COST: 220000
PREDICTION: The temporally consistent transfer learning approach should lead to significant improvements in the model's ability to generalize across different domains and to reason about the temporal evolution of the scene in a more robust and consistent way. However, its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the domains' datasets and the difficulty of the adaptation task.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Temporal Inference for Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Develop an uncertainty-aware temporal inference approach that explicitly models and propagates uncertainty through the temporal dynamics of the satellite image sequence. This will enable the model to reason about the trade-off between temporal consistency and uncertainty and to provide more robust and reliable forecasts.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the uncertainty-aware temporal inference approach with a standard model that ignores uncertainty and a model that uses approximate Bayesian inference.
COST: 270000
PREDICTION: The uncertainty-aware temporal inference approach should lead to significant improvements in the model's ability to reason about the trade-off between temporal consistency and uncertainty and to provide more robust and reliable forecasts. However, its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the uncertainty modeling and the difficulty of the forecasting task.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: A Large-Scale Satellite Image Time Series Dataset for Evaluating Temporal Change Description and Forecasting Models
PROPOSAL: Create a large-scale satellite image time series dataset that contains a diverse range of scenarios and temporal dynamics, including urban expansion, deforestation, and climate-related changes. This dataset will serve as a benchmark for evaluating the performance of models designed for temporal change description and forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: Use the dataset to evaluate the performance of the models proposed in prior research questions and to identify the strengths and weaknesses of each approach.
COST: 330000
PREDICTION: The dataset will provide a comprehensive and challenging benchmark for evaluating the performance of models designed for temporal change description and forecasting tasks. However, its creation and curation may require significant resources and expertise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Examining the Impact of Model Component Adaptation in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experimental study by adapting a pre-trained deep forecasting model for time series prediction, updating either the final prediction layer or a small adapter module, and comparing its performance to the original model on a suite of real-world time series benchmarks from traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting domains.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using the original pre-trained model (no adaptation), and an ablation of updating the adapter module (only updating the final prediction layer).
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The adapted model should improve forecast accuracy, especially in traffic flow forecasting, but may fail to generalize as effectively as the original model on certain types of electricity consumption data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Distribution Shift Normalization in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will design and evaluate a set of normalization strategies specifically tailored for online time series forecasting, including computing normalization statistics individually for each sample and forecasting future statistics from past ones, and test their performance on real-world benchmarks from exchange rate forecasting and weather forecasting domains.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using un-normalized data (consistent with most existing online time series forecasting methods), and an ablation of focusing on statistical normalization (testing the model's performance with more complex normalization methods like autoencoders).
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: These normalization strategies should improve forecast accuracy in real-world time series data, particularly in regimes with strong distribution shifts, but may fail to achieve substantial improvements when the data exhibit moderate levels of concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Development of a One-Step-Ahead Gradient-Based Update Scheme for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a novel online gradient-based update scheme for pre-trained deep forecasting models that allows for the incorporation of delayed feedback and addresses the issue of high variance in gradients estimated from few samples. Our approach involves estimating gradients at each time step based on forecasts from a horizon-step-ahead context window and will be tested on real-world benchmarks from traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and solar power forecasting domains.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using traditional one-sample-per-update online gradient descent (OGD), and an ablation of using a horizon-step-ahead context window (testing the model's performance with a simplified context window size of one time step).
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: This novel update scheme should allow for more reliable adaptation of pre-trained deep forecasting models in the face of delayed and noisy feedback, leading to improved forecast accuracy in multi-step forecasting tasks, but may fail to generalize well when the data exhibit concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparative Evaluation of Different Adapter Module Architectures in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will experimentally investigate the impact of different adapter module architectures, including linear, convolutional, and recurrent adapter modules, in the context of online time series forecasting using pre-trained deep forecasting models. We will evaluate the performance of different adapter modules on real-world benchmarks from electricity transformer temperature forecasting and weather forecasting domains.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using a standard multi-layer perceptron (MLP) as the adapter module, and an ablation of using a frozen adapter module (testing the model's performance withoutadaptation).
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The results should indicate that certain adapter module architectures are better suited for online adaptation in certain domains, but may fail to find a clear winner in all cases, particularly when the data exhibit complex distribution shifts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Stability-Aware Update Strategies for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will design and evaluate stability-aware update strategies for online time series forecasting that ensure the model remains stable and predictable even when adapting to new data. We will test the performance of different update strategies on real-world benchmarks from traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting domains.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using standard online gradient descent (OGD), and an ablation of ignoring stability considerations (testing the model's performance with a more aggressive update schedule).
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The results should indicate that stability-aware update strategies can improve the robustness of online time series forecasting models, reducing the risk of model instability and improving overall performance, but may fail to provide significant gains in regimes with very slow or very fast distribution shifts.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Revision of the One-Step-Ahead Gradient-Based Update Scheme for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will revise the one-step-ahead gradient-based update scheme to incorporate more advanced techniques for reducing the variance of gradient estimates, such as control variate methods and variance reduction techniques from online convex optimization. We will also re-evaluate the performance of the revised scheme on real-world benchmarks from all six domains (traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, electricity transformer temperature forecasting, weather forecasting, solar power forecasting, and exchange rate forecasting).
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using the original one-step-ahead gradient-based update scheme, and an ablation of using variance reduction techniques (testing the model's performance with a simpler update scheme).
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The revised update scheme should provide improved performance and stability for pre-trained deep forecasting models in multi-step forecasting tasks, especially when faced with delayed and noisy feedback, but may fail to adapt well to complex distribution shifts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Online Time Series Forecasting through Transfer Learning and Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: We will explore the use of transfer learning and knowledge transfer techniques to adapt pre-trained models to new time series data, mimicking the process of how humans adapt to new situations based on their existing knowledge. We will test the performance of transfer learning and knowledge transfer techniques on real-world benchmarks from multiple domains using a variety of pre-trained models.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using standard online adaptation (no transfer of knowledge), and an ablation of using transfer learning (testing the model's performance with a naive adaptation approach).
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The results should indicate that transfer learning and knowledge transfer techniques can significantly improve the robustness of online time series forecasting models, allowing them to adapt more effectively to new data and distribution shifts, but may fail to generalize well when applied to very different domains or distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Regret for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will provide a theoretical analysis of the dynamic regret for online time series forecasting algorithms, providing bounds on the performance of these algorithms in various scenarios. We will also investigate the impact of different update schemes, adapter modules, and transfer learning techniques on the dynamic regret using tools from online convex optimization and regret minimization.
CONTROLS: None (theoretical work)

PREDICTION: The results should provide new insights into the relationships between different online time series forecasting techniques and their performance in various scenarios, but may fail to directly evaluate the performance of these techniques on real-world data or in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation of Ensembles for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experimental evaluation of ensembling techniques for online time series forecasting, including bagging, boosting, and stacking, to improve the robustness and accuracy of online time series forecasting models. We will test the performance of different ensembling techniques on real-world benchmarks from all six domains (traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, electricity transformer temperature forecasting, weather forecasting, solar power forecasting, and exchange rate forecasting).
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using a single model (without ensembling), and an ablation of using any ensembling techniques (testing the model's performance with a single model).
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The results should indicate that ensembling techniques can significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of online time series forecasting models, especially when adapted using transfer learning and knowledge transfer, but may fail to provide consistent gains across all domains and distribution shifts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-Scale Exploration of Hyperparameters and Model Architectures for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a large-scale exploration of hyperparameters and model architectures for online time series forecasting using a comprehensive set of publicly available real-world datasets and evaluating performance across all six domains (traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, electricity transformer temperature forecasting, weather forecasting, solar power forecasting, and exchange rate forecasting). We will use techniques such as grid search, random search, and Bayesian optimization to efficiently explore the hyperparameter space.
CONTROLS: This proposal includes two controls: a baseline using a standard hyperparameter setting (consistent with most existing online time series forecasting literature), and an ablation of exploring different model architectures (testing the model's performance with a standard architecture).
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The results should provide insights into the optimal hyperparameters and model architectures for online time series forecasting in each domain, but may be computationally expensive and may not generalize to entirely new or unseen data distributions.

PROPOSAL: Implement the ColPali-based late-interaction multimodal retriever as the primary retriever, paired with a lightweight dense text retriever (RoBERTa-base encoders with bio-embeddings) fine-tuned on a text-based document retrieval dataset (MS MARCO, 30,000 documents).

TITLE: Robust Pseudo-Label Learning with Soft Class Encoding
PROPOSAL: We investigate a novel soft class encoding scheme for pseudo-label learning in semantic segmentation. Specifically, instead of one-hot encoding, we use a Gaussian distribution to model the class confidence. The teacher model generates a class probability vector, and a threshold is applied to obtain a soft pseudo-label with weights that decay with euclidean distance from the mean class probability. TITLE: Frequency-Aware Local Trend Modeling (FLT) Approach
PROPOSAL: Develop an unsupervised detection method for univariate time series, incorporating frequency awareness and local trend modeling to capture and isolate small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies. We propose to use the recent One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) architecture, known for its capacity to learn local patterns, and extend it with Fourier-based components to model periodicity and its evolution over time. A variant of mean interval convergence loss function will be used to evaluate the reliability of predicted local trends.
